label: early original-phase input of 1/l/m/z/x in favorable context (prev z/w/g/l/e/o or first token d/f/c)
explanation: Sparse (~1% of steps) reset-gate unit. 81% of activation mass is in the original phase at t=2..5 (peak t=3, 44% of mass); never active at t=0,1 or at the delimiter. It responds to the current input token (1 and l strongest, then m, z, x) and the response depends on context: the previous token (z, w, g, l, e, o) and especially the first token of the sequence (d gives 6x lift, f/c 3x). The largest activations are sequences starting with d where l is input at t=3 (e.g. d w w [l], d l w [l]). The token set alone has low precision (~0.11) because the same tokens in other contexts usually do not trigger it, so the gating looks like a distributed hidden-state conjunction that a simple predicate only roughly captures. About 19% of mass is in the copy phase (late recall positions 5-8 and fed-back inputs such as 1), and the predicate does not cover it. Dev: P 0.32, R 0.40, F1 0.36, mass recall 0.52.
